Thank you Michael for your insightful and inspiring speech today. Thank you to the pumped up pastor and brothers for starting the day off right!!💪🏻. Thank you Animal Services for all you do. Thank you Jesus for blessing me as you have.

 The Rotary Club of SEQ Wildlife Rescue in District 9640 is a specialised club in South East Queensland dedicated to rescuing, rehabilitating and releasing native Australian wildlife back into the wild.
 In less than a year since being chartered, the club has already released wallabies, gliders, possums, lorikeets and many other birds back into their natural habitat.
 Beyond rescuing animals, the club is training new carers, building relationships with wildlife organisations, working with property developers to protect wildlife during land clearing, and planning a future wildlife hospital and education centre 🌿

HCSO Arrests Man for Assault on First Responder, DUI
 Hamilton County, TN – On the evening of August 6, 2026, HCSO deputies responded to the 3200 block of Ooltewah Ringgold Road regarding an automated crash notification.
 Once on scene, deputies found a flatbed tow truck off the roadway in the bushes with the driver uncommunicative and appearing to be under the influence. The driver, identified as Ric Kennett, did not respond to commands to exit the tow truck.
 Deputies identified multiple weapons on Kennett, including a handgun and two knives, and attempted to assist Kennett with exiting the vehicle. Kennett continued to resist and became violent against law enforcement, also attempting to flee on foot. The suspect was tased and put into restraints.
 Kennett is charged with the following in addition to multiple traffic violations:
 • Assault on First Responder x2
 • Possessing a Firearm with Intent to go Armed
 • Driving Under the Influence 
 • Possession of Handgun while Under the Influence
 • Evading Arrest
 • Resisting Arrest
 We want to thank the Collegedale Police Department and Tri-Community Volunteer Fire Department for their assistance.
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

Deputies identified multiple weapons on Kennett, including a handgun and two knives, and attempted to assist Kennett with exiting the vehicle. Kennett continued to resist and became violent against law enforcement, also attempting to flee on foot. The suspect was tased and put into restraints.
Kennett is charged with the following in addition to multiple traffic violations:
• Assault on First Responder x2
• Possessing a Firearm with Intent to go Armed
• Driving Under the Influence
• Possession of Handgun while Under the Influence
• Evading Arrest
• Resisting Arrest
We want to thank the Collegedale Police Department and Tri-Community Volunteer Fire Department for their assistance.
This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

Chattanooga Police Department welcomes 21 new officers
 CHATTANOOGA, Tenn.  – The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) today celebrated the graduation 21 cadets from its 20-week police academy.
 The members of CPD Class 2026-2 came into the academy with a wide range of life experiences and professional backgrounds, but shared a common goal of serving the Chattanooga community. Among the graduates are four military veterans, a former professional football player, a recruit from the Middle East, two whose siblings already serve with CPD, a former wildland firefighter, a personal trainer, and a welder. 
 "Every officer brings a unique perspective shaped by their own experiences, and that's one of our department's greatest strengths," said Chief John Chambers. "Building a department with people from different backgrounds and professions helps us better understand and serve the diverse community that calls Chattanooga home."
 The new officers will now begin 16 weeks of field training, working alongside experienced CPD Field Training Officers as they transition into patrol assignments.
 The graduation ceremony was held at Abba's House in Hixson. CPD thanks Abba's House for providing the event space to celebrate this milestone for the department's newest officers.
 Congratulations to CPD Academy Class 2026-2!
 #CPDnews

When Dr. Faith Rose received her framed certificate as the first graduate of the Siskin Hospital-UTC Geriatric Physical Therapy Residency Program, the applause was for more than one graduate.
 The graduation ceremony, held Thursday, July 30, at Siskin Hospital for Physical Rehabilitation, marked a personal milestone for Rose, a first for Siskin Hospital and another step toward preparing more specialists to serve older adults in Chattanooga and across Tennessee.
 Rose, who earned her Doctor of Physical Therapy degree from UTC in 2020, completed the 12-month post-professional residency after a year of advanced clinical training, research, teaching and mentorship focused on geriatric care. The program, launched in 2025 through a partnership between UTC and Siskin Hospital, was built to meet a need that leaders in both organizations say is only becoming more urgent as the population ages.

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
 August 6th, 2026
 Hamilton County Health Department & Community Partners to Host 2026 Red Sand Project to Raise Awareness of Human Trafficking
 HAMILTON COUNTY, TN— The Hamilton County Health and Social Services Division, WillowBend Farms, the Dr. Carol B. Berz Family Justice Center, Vision Hospitality Group, and other community organizations will host the 2026 Chattanooga Red Sand Project on Friday, August 7. This event aims to raise awareness about human trafficking and unite the community in support of survivors. It is part of a statewide initiative involving all 95 counties in Tennessee.
 During the Red Sand Project, interactive and visual displays will help participants learn more about human trafficking, modern slavery, and exploitation, while also acknowledging those who often go unnoticed in society. The project encourages community members to recognize the signs of human trafficking, understand its impact, and actively participate in prevention and support for survivors.
 “The Red Sand Project serves as a powerful reminder that no community is immune to human trafficking. The red sand placed in sidewalk cracks symbolizes the victims and survivors whose experiences are often overlooked,” said Beka Bohannon, Administrator of Hamilton County Health and Social Services. “The Health Department is committed to combating human trafficking and proudly collaborates with local leaders such as WillowBend Farms and the Vision Hospitality Group to support survivors. Together, we can demonstrate that human trafficking has no place in Hamilton County.”
 According to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, human trafficking is a crime driven by demand that involves the exploitation of individuals for labor, services, or commercial sex acts. This crime affects men, women, and children alike. Human trafficking is one of the fastest-growing criminal industries in the United States, with cases reported in all 50 states. The National Human Trafficking Hotline reported that in 2024, Tennessee had 213 cases of human trafficking, involving a total of 446 victims, as each case can include multiple victims.
 “This year's Red Sand Project is set to be one of our best. We are not only raising awareness about the significant impacts in the fight against human trafficking in the Chattanooga area, but we are also placing survivor voices at the forefront of this year's event,” said Sarah McKinnis, CEO and Founder of WillowBend Farms Inc. “There is no greater influence in leading this fight than those who are willing to stand up and share their stories about the freedom available to victims who courageously step forward and inspire others. As we celebrate 250 years of freedom in the United States, this event will highlight how that foundation has led to generational freedom right here in Chattanooga.”
 Event Details:
 Friday, August 7, 2026
 Program begins at 10 a.m.
 Aloft by Marriott Chattanooga Hamilton Place
 2090 Hamilton Place Blvd., Chattanooga, TN 37421
 “Vision Hospitality Group is once again proud to host our 6th annual Red Sand Event at the Aloft Hotel at Hamilton Place. When we first collaborated with various incredible groups and businesses in Chattanooga to combat the horrifying crime of human trafficking, we could never have imagined how much this partnership would grow,” said Jenelle Hawkins, Director of Operational Excellence at Vision Hospitality Group. “The impact of our collective efforts is truly making a difference in our community. This year’s theme for the Red Sand Event focuses on how everyday people can continue to contribute to this important cause, and we at Vision are excited to see Chattanooga come together once again.”
 If you know someone who needs help to escape trafficking, contact the Tennessee Human Trafficking
 Hotline at 1-855-558-6484. If you suspect you have encountered a victim of human trafficking, you may
 call the National Human Trafficking Hotline at 1-888-373-7888 or text 233733.
 As part of our outreach efforts to raise awareness about human trafficking, there will be a Red Sand Project Networking event on Friday, August 7th, following the press conference. Due to limited space, please RSVP. You can find all event information and the RSVP link at: [Eventbrite](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/red-sand-project-chattanooga-t…).
 Additional resources
 Questions? Call the Health Department at 423-209-8000.
 Free interpretation services are available at all Health Department clinics.
 For Health Department information, visit: Health.HamiltonTN.org
 To read this information in Spanish, visit the Health Department’s Spanish Facebook page at https://www.facebook.com/SaludHamiltonTN

Tennessee's hospitality industry had another banner year. The Tennessee Department of Tourist Development released statewide numbers: a record $32.5 billion in direct visitor spending, up 2.7% over 2024 and beating the national growth rate. We're glad to be part of it, and grateful to our partners and community who make Chattanooga a place people want to visit!
 #VisitChatt #chattanooga #TDTD Industry
The Tennessee Department of Tourist Development announced the 2025 State Economic Impact today at the Appalachian Clubhouse in Great Smoky Mountains National Park. Tennessee’s tourism industry reached a record-breaking $32.5 billion in direct visitor spending in 2025, an increase of 2.7% over the previous year and higher than the national average growth rate of 1.9%. Since 2018, Tennessee's tourism economy has grown 40%, nearly double the national growth rate of 22%.
 Great Smoky Mountains National Park provided the perfect backdrop for this announcement, commemorating its role as a cornerstone of Tennessee’s tourism success. Last fall, state, city, and local leaders worked alongside federal partners to keep the Smokies open for 40 days, allowing more than 2.4 million people to visit during that time.
 This continued growth is a direct result of Tennessee’s strong partnerships, dedicated leaders, and one-of-a-kind destinations that create unforgettable moments for visitors from around the world and continue to strengthen Tennessee’s reputation as a world-class destination.
 The full 2025 Economic Impact of Travel Report and direct visitor spending data for all 95 counties will be released in September. 
 The statewide report, including methodology, can be found here: https://industry.tnvacation.com/industry/research
 All data is sourced from the Tennessee Department of Tourist Development and Tourism Economics, with national benchmarks provided by the U.S. Travel Association.

The Tennessee Department of Tourist Development released statewide numbers: a record $32.5 billion in direct visitor spending, up 2.7% over 2024 and beating the national growth rate. We're glad to be part of it, and grateful to our partners and community who make Chattanooga a place people want to visit!
#VisitChatt #chattanooga #TDTD Industry
The Tennessee Department of Tourist Development announced the 2025 State Economic Impact today at the Appalachian Clubhouse in Great Smoky Mountains National Park. Tennessee’s tourism industry reached a record-breaking $32.5 billion in direct visitor spending in 2025, an increase of 2.7% over the previous year and higher than the national average growth rate of 1.9%. Since 2018, Tennessee's tourism economy has grown 40%, nearly double the national growth rate of 22%.
Great Smoky Mountains National Park provided the perfect backdrop for this announcement, commemorating its role as a cornerstone of Tennessee’s tourism success. Last fall, state, city, and local leaders worked alongside federal partners to keep the Smokies open for 40 days, allowing more than 2.4 million people to visit during that time.
This continued growth is a direct result of Tennessee’s strong partnerships, dedicated leaders, and one-of-a-kind destinations that create unforgettable moments for visitors from around the world and continue to strengthen Tennessee’s reputation as a world-class destination.
The full 2025 Economic Impact of Travel Report and direct visitor spending data for all 95 counties will be released in September.
The statewide report, including methodology, can be found here: https://industry.tnvacation.com/industry/research
All data is sourced from the Tennessee Department of Tourist Development and Tourism Economics, with national benchmarks provided by the U.S. Travel Association.

Today is the day to #ArtsVote!
ArtsBuild Launches Arts Voter Guide for Hamilton County Elections - Check it Out at the Link Below!
 CHATTANOOGA, TN – ArtsBuild has released its 2026 Arts Voter Guide, a nonpartisan resource highlighting where Hamilton County candidates stand on arts and culture. The guide features responses from candidates for Hamilton County Mayor, County Commission, and School Board.
 With early voting beginning July 17 and Election Day on August 6, ArtsBuild encourages voters to learn where candidates stand on issues affecting the arts. Hamilton County's nonprofit arts and culture sector employs more than 3,000 people and generates nearly $200 million in annual economic activity while enriching education, strengthening neighborhoods, and expanding access to creative opportunities.
 "The Arts Voter Guide is a resource for every Hamilton County voter," said ArtsBuild President James McKissic. "Our goal is to provide voters with the information they need to make informed decisions and better understand each candidate's perspective on the role of the arts in our community."
 As part of its mission to build stronger communities through the arts, ArtsBuild supports the nonprofit arts sector and advocates for arts education and access throughout Chattanooga and Hamilton County. The Arts Voter Guide is designed to help voters make informed decisions while remaining strictly nonpartisan.
 The guide is available now at artsbuild.com/advocacy.
 About ArtsBuild
 ArtsBuild is a Chattanooga-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to building stronger communities through the arts. Since 1969, ArtsBuild has invested more than $80 million in Hamilton County through grants to arts organizations, arts education programs for students and teachers, and initiatives that expand access to the arts for all residents.  Support our work at: https://secure.qgiv.com/for/aaogc/

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
 August 6th, 2026
 Hamilton County Health Department & Community Partners to Host 2026 Red Sand Project to Raise Awareness of Human Trafficking
 HAMILTON COUNTY, TN— The Hamilton County Health and Social Services Division, WillowBend Farms, the Dr. Carol B. Berz Family Justice Center, Vision Hospitality Group, and other community organizations will host the 2026 Chattanooga Red Sand Project on Friday, August 7. This event aims to raise awareness about human trafficking and unite the community in support of survivors. It is part of a statewide initiative involving all 95 counties in Tennessee.
 During the Red Sand Project, interactive and visual displays will help participants learn more about human trafficking, modern slavery, and exploitation, while also acknowledging those who often go unnoticed in society. The project encourages community members to recognize the signs of human trafficking, understand its impact, and actively participate in prevention and support for survivors.
 “The Red Sand Project serves as a powerful reminder that no community is immune to human trafficking. The red sand placed in sidewalk cracks symbolizes the victims and survivors whose experiences are often overlooked,” said Beka Bohannon, Administrator of Hamilton County Health and Social Services. “The Health Department is committed to combating human trafficking and proudly collaborates with local leaders such as WillowBend Farms and the Vision Hospitality Group to support survivors. Together, we can demonstrate that human trafficking has no place in Hamilton County.”
 According to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, human trafficking is a crime driven by demand that involves the exploitation of individuals for labor, services, or commercial sex acts. This crime affects men, women, and children alike. Human trafficking is one of the fastest-growing criminal industries in the United States, with cases reported in all 50 states. The National Human Trafficking Hotline reported that in 2024, Tennessee had 213 cases of human trafficking, involving a total of 446 victims, as each case can include multiple victims.
 “This year's Red Sand Project is set to be one of our best. We are not only raising awareness about the significant impacts in the fight against human trafficking in the Chattanooga area, but we are also placing survivor voices at the forefront of this year's event,” said Sarah McKinnis, CEO and Founder of WillowBend Farms Inc. “There is no greater influence in leading this fight than those who are willing to stand up and share their stories about the freedom available to victims who courageously step forward and inspire others. As we celebrate 250 years of freedom in the United States, this event will highlight how that foundation has led to generational freedom right here in Chattanooga.”
 Event Details:
 • Friday, August 7, 2026
 • Program begins at 10 a.m.
 • Aloft by Marriott Chattanooga Hamilton Place
 • 2090 Hamilton Place Blvd., Chattanooga, TN 37421
 “Vision Hospitality Group is once again proud to host our 6th annual Red Sand Event at the Aloft Hotel at Hamilton Place. When we first collaborated with various incredible groups and businesses in Chattanooga to combat the horrifying crime of human trafficking, we could never have imagined how much this partnership would grow,” said Jenelle Hawkins, Director of Operational Excellence at Vision Hospitality Group. “The impact of our collective efforts is truly making a difference in our community. This year’s theme for the Red Sand Event focuses on how everyday people can continue to contribute to this important cause, and we at Vision are excited to see Chattanooga come together once again.”
 If you know someone who needs help to escape trafficking, contact the Tennessee Human Trafficking
 Hotline at 1-855-558-6484. If you suspect you have encountered a victim of human trafficking, you may
 call the National Human Trafficking Hotline at 1-888-373-7888 or text 233733.
 As part of our outreach efforts to raise awareness about human trafficking, there will be a Red Sand Project Networking event on Friday, August 7th, following the press conference. Due to limited space, please RSVP. You can find all event information and the RSVP link at: [Eventbrite](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/red-sand-project-chattanooga-t…).
 Additional resources 
 • Questions? Call the Health Department at 423-209-8000.
 • Free interpretation services are available at all Health Department clinics. 
 • For Health Department information, visit: Health.HamiltonTN.org
 • To read this information in Spanish, visit the Health Department’s Spanish Facebook page at https://www.facebook.com/SaludHamiltonTN

Preserving Black Churches Grant Program Now Open: Apply today!
 As the oldest institutions created and controlled by African Americans, historically Black churches are a living testament to the achievements and resiliency of generations of American families and communities.
 To preserve and uplift these historic places and the neighborhoods they serve, the Preserving Black Churches grant program provides funding ranging from $50,000 to $500,000.
 Do you know of a congregation in your community that could use support? No church is too small. No town is too remote.
 The Preserving Black Churches grant program is a cornerstone initiative of the African American Cultural Heritage Action Fund at @NationalTrustforHistoricPreservation. Since its first cohort in 2023, this program has provided $8.5 million in funding to support critical preservation work including building repair and programming interpretation that elevates the significance of the historically Black church’s cultural legacy.
 Applications due September 11 at 5:00 p.m. ET.
 Learn more: https://savingplaces.org/black-churches
  #preservationgrants #preservationgrantsprogram

items.content_text:
Official development assistance (ODA) to sub-Saharan Africa and least developed countries is projected to decline again in 2026.
 An #OECD policy brief projects a third consecutive year of decline in bilateral ODA to sub-Saharan Africa and least developed countries, bringing support to its lowest level since the early 2000s.
 ➡️ Bilateral ODA to sub-Saharan Africa could decline by 11.6% in 2026
 ➡️ Least developed countries could see a decline of 10.9% 
 The projected declines follow significant reductions in 2025, when ODA to sub-Saharan Africa and least developed countries fell by 26.3% and 25.8% respectively.
 The policy brief also notes that many of the countries most exposed to the current contraction rely on a limited number of providers for development finance, increasing their vulnerability to reductions in ODA.
 Multilateral ODA is also projected to decline in 2026, limiting the ability of international organisations to help offset reductions in bilateral aid. 
 Read the policy brief: https://brnw.ch/21x4HUe
 #ODA2026 #OECDdevelopment

Two weeks ago, our AAAD team was proud to participate in the 36th Annual Americans with Disabilities Act Celebration hosted by the City of Chattanooga Mayor's Council on Disability. The event brought together organizations from across our community that are working every day to expand access, remove barriers, and create opportunities for individuals with disabilities.

From learning about Harrison Bay State Park's Access 2030 initiative to connecting with organizations like Special Olympics, the National Federation of the Blind, Partnership for Deaf Services, the American Job Center, and many others, the day highlighted the incredible impact that collaboration can have across our region.

Thank you to the City of Chattanooga Mayor's Council on Disability for bringing our community together to celebrate the progress we've made and to continue advancing accessibility and inclusion for all.

At SETD, we're proud to support initiatives that strengthen our communities and improve quality of life for the people we serve!

From learning about Harrison Bay State Park's Access 2030 initiative to connecting with organizations like Special Olympics, the National Federation of the Blind, Partnership for Deaf Services, the American Job Center, and many others, the day highlighted the incredible impact that collaboration can have across our region. Thank you to the City of Chattanooga Mayor's Council on Disability for bringing our community together to celebrate the progress we've made and to continue advancing accessibility and inclusion for all. At SETD, we're proud to support initiatives that strengthen our communities and improve quality of life for the people we serve!

 After more than two years of restoration, the historic Tivoli Theatre is set to reopen this October, welcoming audiences back to one of our city's most treasured landmarks.
 The Tivoli has been at the heart of Chattanooga's cultural life for more than a century, proving that investing in our historic places doesn't just preserve the past, it creates vibrant spaces for our future.
 At Preserve Chattanooga, we celebrate projects like this because every restored historic building strengthens our community, supports our local economy, and keeps Chattanooga's unique story alive.
 Congratulations to everyone who made this remarkable restoration possible. We can't wait to see the lights come back on at the "Jewel of the South."
 Read the full story from The Pulse: https://www.chattanoogapulse.com/…/historic-tivoli-theatre…/

A huge THANK YOU to Family Forward for inviting the Office of Early Learning to speak with families during your parent workshop! 💙 We loved sharing one of our favorite reminders:
 💡 You don’t have to add more to your day to prepare your child for kindergarten, you just have to make the most of the moments you’re already living.
 Turn everyday tasks into learning adventures:
 🥕 Count vegetables while cooking.
 🧦 Match socks on laundry day.
 🍎 Name the colors of fruits at the grocery store.
 🥣 Read cereal boxes together over breakfast.
 🚗 Count stop signs, sing the ABCs, and talk about what you see on the way to the store.
 The best classroom is often the one you create in everyday life. ❤️
 Keep it simple. Make it fun. Let it fit your family’s routine. Those little moments add up to BIG learning!
 Because families are a child’s first teachers and every moment is a chance to learn. 🌟
